{"id": "c4def619-8031-4bb5-b642-06f4bba803c0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Comparing the two VIFs: 192.168.1.0/24 is advertised only on VIF-A, with no matching route on VIF-B.

**What's at risk:** If VIF-A (or the Direct Connect connection/path it rides on) fails, traffic to **192.168.1.0/24 has no failover path** — VIF-B can't take over for that prefix since it never advertises it. Everything else (10.10.0.0/24 and 10.10.1.0/24) is covered on both VIFs, so those subnets would fail over cleanly.

To close the gap, 192.168.1.0/24 needs to also be advertised on VIF-B (or on whatever the true redundant path is for that VIF).

A couple of things worth checking to be sure this assessment is complete:", "type": "text"}, {"id": "tooluse_enhJifSiqodxk3wfrTh6kd", "tool_name": "ask_user", "input": {"question": "Want me to dig deeper into this DX setup?", "options": [{"label": "Check VIF/connection details in AWS", "description": "Look up the actual Direct Connect VIFs and connections in your account", "recommended": true, "recommended_reason": "Confirms whether VIF-A and VIF-B sit on physically redundant connections"}, {"label": "Check BGP route propagation", "description": "Verify whether 192.168.1.0/24 is actually being learned/advertised as expected"}]}, "type": "tool_use"}], "created_at": null}
